statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low at 4 because CME equity index futures remain halted for the weekend and no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists inside any hour of this 24-hour horizon; Stress is moderate at 36, carrying an unchanged rates, energy and US-Iran position from Friday's settlement.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion: cash NDX retraced both of its extremes, closed below its own open, and left VIX near session lows, while the August expiry cleared without one-way extension. The venue has been shut since 21:00Z on Friday and reopens on Sunday at 22:00Z, roughly twenty hours beyond the end of this horizon, so the published Tail describes the absence of a price path rather than an improvement in the backdrop. Re-verification during this hour cross-checked Friday's close against a second independent source after one quote provider returned a stale Nasdaq-100 level, and confirmed VIX at 14.89, the 2Y/10Y/30Y curve at 4.24%/4.74%/5.28%, WTI at 87.06 and Brent at 94.39 unchanged. It also confirmed the week-ahead catalyst stack: Core PCE and the second Q2 GDP estimate on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close, and Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, against roughly 35% pricing for a September rate increase and about 66% by December. Those are dated checkpoints beyond this horizon and inform Stress, not current Tail. No danger window is published because no tradable window exists.
headline: Fifth consecutive closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across every published hour, with Friday's cash NDX close of 29,308.86, +0.33%, re-verified against a second source after a stale third-party quote.
body: CME equity index futures stopped trading for the week at 21:00Z on Friday and reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run to 2026-08-23T02:00:00Z. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60, trading down to 29,142.44, reclaiming the entire decline to 29,405.12 and then handing back roughly ninety-six points to finish below its own open. Both extremes were retraced, neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, and the August expiry cleared without one-way structure. One quote provider returned a materially different Nasdaq-100 level during this run while displaying its own delayed-data warning; the settlement above was confirmed independently, including a 29,213.16 close on 20 August, and the divergent figure was discarded. That close snapped a five-day Nasdaq-100 losing streak, though the index still ended the week about 2% lower and the semiconductor complex about 5% lower. VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the base of a 14.77-15.95 range. The carried rates position is unchanged: 2Y 4.24%, 10Y 4.74% testing 20-month highs, and 30Y 5.28% close to its highest level since 2007. Crude is elevated but stable at WTI 87.06 and Brent 94.39 with Strait of Hormuz traffic restricted since early July and no new supply break. Delayed cross-asset context from the last session shows two-sided megacap dispersion, five of eight higher with Tesla the outlier, and mixed semiconductor breadth with four of seven lower, which argues against carrying a directional prior. The US-Iran file hardened rhetorically into the weekend without accompanying transmission, so it sits in Stress. With no exchange open, shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension and session-extreme holding are all unobservable, and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor of 4 for every slot.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 19 hourly assessments are available and 5 clock-hours, all in the 21 August overnight and late-morning windows, have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-16 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout. The path is coherent: 12 through the early European morning, a drift to 16 into the 14:00Z US cash-open window with a brief event/whipsaw mode around the August expiry, a return to the low teens through the afternoon, then a step down to 10, 5 and finally 4 as the venue moved into its 21:00Z Friday halt and stayed there. Stress traced the same arc in reverse scale, easing from the high fifties to the mid thirties as equity-structure risk was replaced by carried rates, energy and weekend headline risk. No danger window was published in any of those hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the horizon ends at 2026-08-23T02:00:00Z, roughly twenty hours before the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds a flat closed-venue floor of 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON in every slot. Stress eases from 36 to a 34 trough through the quietest weekend hours and then climbs back to 42 by the final slot as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows and the distance to the reopen shortens; its composition is unchanged, with the 30-year at 5.28% near a 2007 high, the 10-year at 4.74% testing 20-month highs, crude held near 87.06 WTI and 94.39 Brent, and an unresolved US-Iran impasse. Confidence eases gently from 85 to 79 with forecast distance rather than because current evidence is thin. The dated checkpoints that matter, Core PCE and Q2 GDP on Wednesday, Nvidia after the Wednesday close and the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote on Friday, all fall beyond this horizon and are reflected in Stress rather than in Tail.
